name: How high can a second story be in Pasadena or Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: What height limits or zoning constraints can stop a second-story addition from being approved in Pasadena, Los Angeles, or nearby cities?
mainEntity.text: What height limits or zoning constraints can stop a second-story addition from being approved in Pasadena, Los Angeles, or nearby cities?

acceptedAnswer.text: Height is one of the biggest zoning issues for second-story additions because a new upper floor can quickly exceed what the property is allowed to build. Local rules may limit overall building height, ridge height, attic conversions, and how close the upper story can come to the front, side, or rear property lines. In some neighborhoods, approval also depends on neighborhood compatibility, massing, or preservation-related review. Pasadena and parts of Los Angeles can be especially sensitive to scale and context, so even a technically buildable design may need revisions to reduce visual bulk or improve setbacks. Homeowners should also watch for special districts, hillside rules, and historic or overlay requirements that can affect height in ways that are not obvious from a standard zoning summary. Before finalizing the design, it is smart to confirm what the maximum envelope is and whether the project triggers additional review beyond ordinary building permit approval.
acceptedAnswer.description: Height limits, setbacks, lot coverage, and neighborhood compatibility rules can all affect whether a second-story addition is approved. In some areas, the design must also match block scale, preserve street character, or meet special overlay requirements before permit approval.
